title: Filter Passing Scores
prompt: A gradebook only wants to show scores that pass the current threshold. Write a function that returns a new array containing scores greater than or equal to the passing score, preserving their original order.

explanation.beginner:
Example: filterPassingScores([72,88,59,90], 70) produces [72,88,90]. For each score, evaluate the inclusive threshold. Keep the score itself when the predicate is true, in original order.

Compare “keeps values equal to the threshold”: input [[60,61,59],60] produces [60,61]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
For each score, evaluate the inclusive threshold. Keep the score itself when the predicate is true, in original order.

Tempting mistake: map(score => score >= 80) returns booleans for every score. filter keeps the matching scores.

The reference uses filter. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost. One pass costs O(n) time; the output stores up to n values.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “keeps values equal to the threshold”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
